cashTip: Cards and phone payments work almost everywhere; prices are in francs, and euros get a poor rate.
name: Lucerne
tagline: A medieval lakeside town ringed by mountains
summary: Lucerne is postcard Switzerland: a covered wooden bridge, painted old-town squares and a lake framed by Mount Pilatus and Rigi. Cruise the lake on paddle steamers, ride the world's steepest cogwheel railway and visit the Lion Monument.
seasonNote: Summer is best for lakes and mountains. December has Christmas markets; Carnival (Fasnacht) is wild in February.
arrival: Trains from Zurich take about 45 minutes, and from Zurich Airport about an hour.
gettingAround: Walk the old town; boats, trains and cable cars for the mountains. The Swiss Travel Pass covers most.
foodTip: Luzerner Chügelipastete vol-au-vent, fondue and rösti.
buyTip: Swiss watches, chocolate and army knives.
baseArea: Old town or by the lake

connections.note: Luzern–Interlaken Express over the Brünig Pass.

items.name: Chapel Bridge
items.summary: A 14th-century covered wooden bridge with painted panels and a water tower.

items.name: Old town and Musegg Wall
items.summary: Frescoed squares and medieval walls with towers you can climb.

items.name: Lion Monument
items.summary: A dying lion carved into a cliff, honouring Swiss Guards killed in 1792.
items.why: Mark Twain called it the saddest stone.

items.name: Mount Pilatus
items.summary: The 'Golden Round Trip': boat, the world's steepest cogwheel railway up, cable cars down.
items.tip: Do the full golden round trip.

items.name: Mount Rigi
items.summary: The 'queen of the mountains', with Europe's first mountain railway and lake views.

items.name: Lake Lucerne cruise
items.summary: Paddle steamers through fjord-like arms of the lake.

items.name: Swiss Museum of Transport
items.summary: Trains, planes, cars and a planetarium; Switzerland's most visited museum.

items.name: Mount Titlis
items.summary: A rotating cable car to glaciers, an ice cave and Europe's highest suspension bridge.
items.expect: Cold at the top all year.

items.name: Luzerner Chügelipastete
items.summary: A puff-pastry case filled with veal, mushrooms and cream sauce.
items.tip: Order it in a guild house.

items.name: Cheese fondue
items.summary: Melted cheese with bread, best on a cold evening.

items.name: Rösti
items.summary: Crispy grated potato cakes, often topped with egg or cheese.

cashTip: Cards and phone payments work almost everywhere; prices are in francs, and euros get a poor rate.
name: Interlaken
tagline: Gateway to the Jungfrau, waterfalls and Alpine thrills
summary: Interlaken sits between two turquoise lakes below the Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau. It's the base for the train to Jungfraujoch, the waterfall valley of Lauterbrunnen, cliffside villages, Grindelwald's cliff walks and adventure sports like paragliding.
seasonNote: Summer is best for hiking. Winter brings skiing in Grindelwald and Wengen. Clouds can hide the peaks; check webcams.
arrival: Trains from Zurich, Bern and Lucerne take 1 to 2 hours.
gettingAround: Mountain trains, cable cars and buses; the Berner Oberland Pass or Swiss Travel Pass saves money.
foodTip: Fondue, raclette, Älplermagronen and Swiss chocolate.
baseArea: Interlaken, or Lauterbrunnen and Wengen for views

items.name: Jungfraujoch
items.summary: The 'Top of Europe': a railway through the Eiger to a 3,454 m saddle with glacier views and an ice palace.
items.expect: Expensive; book ahead and check the weather.

items.name: Lauterbrunnen valley
items.summary: A deep valley with 72 waterfalls, including the famous Staubbach Falls.
items.tip: Walk to Staubbach Falls at dusk.

items.name: Trümmelbach Falls
items.summary: Glacier waterfalls thundering inside a mountain, reached by a lift.

items.name: Grindelwald First
items.summary: A cable car to cliff walks, zip lines and a hike to Bachalpsee lake.

items.name: Harder Kulm
items.summary: A funicular to a viewpoint over both lakes and the Jungfrau peaks.

items.name: Lake Brienz and Iseltwald
items.summary: A turquoise lake with boats to the pretty village of Iseltwald.
items.expect: Iseltwald charges a small fee at its pier.
items.tip: Take the boat to Giessbach falls.

items.name: Schilthorn
items.summary: A revolving summit restaurant made famous by a James Bond film.

items.name: Paragliding
items.summary: Tandem flights from Beatenberg landing in town.

items.name: Raclette
items.summary: Melted cheese scraped over potatoes and pickles.

items.name: Älplermagronen
items.summary: Alpine macaroni with potatoes, cheese, cream and apple sauce.
items.tip: Have it at a mountain hut.

items.name: Swiss chocolate
items.summary: Chocolate shops and workshops.

cashTip: Cards and phone payments work almost everywhere; prices are in francs, and euros get a poor rate.
name: Zermatt
tagline: A car-free village beneath the Matterhorn
summary: Zermatt is a car-free Alpine village of wooden chalets beneath the Matterhorn, Switzerland's most famous peak. Ride the Gornergrat railway, walk past lakes that mirror the mountain, ski year-round on the glacier and dine in mountain huts.
seasonNote: Winter is for skiing; summer for hiking (July to September). Glacier skiing runs all year. Many places close in May and November.
arrival: Cars stop at Täsch; take the shuttle train. Trains from Visp take about an hour, and the Glacier Express links St. Moritz.
gettingAround: Walk, electric taxis and mountain railways.
baseArea: Village centre with a Matterhorn view

items.name: Gornergrat railway
items.summary: A cogwheel railway to 3,089 m with the Matterhorn and 29 peaks over 4,000 m.
items.expect: Sit on the right going up.

items.name: Matterhorn Glacier Paradise
items.summary: Europe's highest cable car station at 3,883 m with a glacier palace.

items.name: Five Lakes walk
items.summary: A trail past five lakes with Matterhorn reflections.

items.name: Riffelsee
items.summary: A small lake mirroring the Matterhorn.
items.tip: Go early when the water is still.

items.name: Matterhorn Museum
items.summary: The story of the first ascent and its tragedy, in a recreated village.

items.name: Hinterdorf old village
items.summary: Old larch-wood barns on stone stilts against mice.

items.name: Gorner Gorge
items.summary: Wooden walkways through a narrow glacier-carved gorge.
items.tip: Combine with a walk to Furi.

items.name: Mountain hut raclette
items.summary: Melted cheese at huts with Matterhorn views.

items.name: Rösti
items.summary: Golden potato rösti with cheese and ham.

items.name: Valais wine
items.summary: Local Fendant whites and Cornalin reds.

cashTip: Cards and phone payments work almost everywhere; prices are in francs, and euros get a poor rate.
name: Geneva
tagline: Lakeside diplomacy, science and the Jet d'Eau
summary: Geneva is a polished lakeside city, home to the UN, the Red Cross and CERN's particle physics lab. Its 140 m Jet d'Eau fountain, old town on the hill and views of Mont Blanc make it a gateway to the Alps.
seasonNote: Summer is warm with lake swimming and the Fêtes de Genève. Winter is grey but has Christmas markets and nearby skiing.
arrival: Geneva Airport is 7 minutes from the centre by train. TGVs from Paris take about 3 hours.
gettingAround: Trams, buses and lake shuttles; hotel guests get a free transport card.
foodTip: Fondue, lake perch fillets, chocolate and Swiss wine.

items.name: Jet d'Eau
items.summary: A 140 m fountain shooting from the lake, Geneva's icon.
items.expect: You'll get wet on the jetty.

items.name: Old town and St Pierre Cathedral
items.summary: Cobbled streets around a cathedral with towers to climb and Roman ruins below.

items.name: Palais des Nations
items.summary: Guided tours of the UN's European headquarters.
items.expect: Bring your passport; book a tour.

items.name: CERN Science Gateway
items.summary: Free exhibitions and tours at the home of the Large Hadron Collider.

items.name: Red Cross Museum
items.wiki: International Red Cross and Red Crescent Museum
items.summary: A moving museum on humanitarian work.
flow: Walk through the three themed zones.
Finish with the archive of prisoner cards.

items.name: Reformation Wall
items.summary: Giant statues of Calvin and other reformers.
items.tip: Watch giant chess in the park.

items.name: Lake Geneva boats
items.summary: Belle Époque paddle steamers to Lausanne, Montreux and Yvoire.
items.tip: Sail to Yvoire, a medieval French village.

items.name: Chamonix and Aiguille du Midi
items.summary: A cable car to 3,842 m facing Mont Blanc, in France.
items.expect: About 1.5 hours by road; bring your passport.
items.tip: Step into the Void glass box.

items.name: Fondue
items.summary: Gruyère and vacherin fondue in a cosy old-town restaurant.
items.tip: Try it at Café du Soleil.

items.name: Lake perch fillets
items.summary: Fried perch fillets with lemon butter and fries.

items.name: Chocolatiers
items.summary: Historic chocolate shops and pavés de Genève.

cashTip: Cards and contactless work almost everywhere; a little cash helps in rural pubs and markets.
name: Galway
tagline: Music pubs, the Wild Atlantic Way and the Cliffs of Moher
summary: Galway is Ireland's most bohemian city, with buskers on Shop Street, trad music in every pub and festivals all year. It's the base for the Cliffs of Moher, the Burren, the Aran Islands and the wild landscapes of Connemara.
seasonNote: Summer brings the Arts Festival and Galway Races. Expect rain any time. Winters are mild but windy.
arrival: Trains from Dublin take about 2.5 hours. Shannon Airport is 1.5 hours away.
gettingAround: Walk the centre; tours or a car for the Cliffs and Connemara.
foodTip: Galway Bay oysters, seafood chowder and fish and chips.
buyTip: Claddagh rings, Aran sweaters and Irish whiskey.

items.name: Latin Quarter and Shop Street
items.summary: Colourful pedestrian streets of buskers, shops and pubs.

items.name: Spanish Arch
items.summary: A 16th-century arch by the river mouth, with swans and the Long Walk.
items.tip: Sit by the river at sunset.

items.name: Trad music sessions
items.summary: Fiddles and flutes in pubs like Tig Cóilí.
items.expect: Sessions start around 6 pm and 9:30 pm.

items.name: Cliffs of Moher
items.summary: Cliffs rising 214 m above the Atlantic.
items.tip: Walk the cliff path toward Hag's Head.

items.name: The Burren
items.summary: A limestone moonscape with rare flowers and the Poulnabrone dolmen.
items.expect: On the way to the Cliffs.

items.name: Aran Islands (Inis Mór)
items.summary: Stone walls, cliff fort Dún Aonghasa and Irish-speaking villages.
items.tip: Rent a bike on the island.

items.name: Kylemore Abbey and Connemara
items.summary: A lakeside abbey and Victorian garden amid Connemara's mountains.
items.expect: Long drive; a tour is easiest.

items.name: Galway Cathedral
items.summary: A grand 1960s cathedral with a green dome.
flow: Step inside and let your eyes adjust.
Look up at the vaulting and windows.

items.name: Galway Bay oysters
items.summary: Native oysters with brown bread and stout.

items.name: Seafood chowder
items.summary: Creamy fish and shellfish soup with brown bread.

items.name: Fish and chips
items.summary: Battered fish and chips by the river.

cashTip: Cards and contactless work almost everywhere; a little cash helps in rural pubs and markets.
name: Killarney
tagline: Lakes, mountains and the Ring of Kerry
summary: Killarney is a lively market town beside a national park of lakes, mountains and waterfalls. It's the starting point for the Ring of Kerry drive, the Gap of Dunloe and trips to Dingle and the Skellig Islands.
seasonNote: Summer is busiest. Spring and autumn are quieter and green. Skellig boats run mid-May to September.
arrival: Trains from Dublin take about 3.5 hours. Kerry Airport is 15 minutes away.
gettingAround: Jaunting cars, bikes and tours; a car for the Ring of Kerry.
foodTip: Irish stew, Kerry lamb, soda bread and a full Irish breakfast.
buyTip: Kerry wool, Irish whiskey and pottery.

connections.note: Usually with a change at Mallow.

items.name: Killarney National Park
items.summary: Lakes, oak woods and red deer at the foot of Ireland's highest mountains.
items.tip: Rent a bike or take a jaunting car.

items.name: Muckross House
items.summary: A Victorian mansion with gardens and traditional farms.

items.name: Ross Castle
items.summary: A 15th-century tower house on the lake, with boat trips.

items.name: Gap of Dunloe
items.summary: A mountain pass walked, cycled or crossed by pony and trap, returning by boat.
items.tip: Do the bike and boat combo.

items.name: Torc Waterfall
items.summary: A 20 m waterfall in mossy woods.
items.expect: Short walk from the car park.
items.tip: Climb the steps above for the view.

items.name: Ring of Kerry
items.summary: A 179 km loop of coastal cliffs, villages and mountain views.
items.expect: Coaches drive anticlockwise; cars often go clockwise.
items.tip: Stop at Ladies View and Derrynane.

items.name: Dingle
items.summary: A harbour town of pubs and music, with the Slea Head drive.

items.name: Skellig Michael
items.summary: A rocky island with 6th-century beehive monastery huts, used in Star Wars.
items.expect: Boats are limited and weather-dependent; book months ahead.

items.name: Irish stew
items.summary: Lamb, potato and carrot stew.

items.name: Full Irish breakfast
items.summary: Eggs, rashers, sausages, black and white pudding.

items.name: Soda bread and scones
items.summary: Brown soda bread and scones with butter and jam.

cashTip: Cards work almost everywhere; carry a few euros for fries stands and markets.
name: Ghent
tagline: Medieval towers and canals with a student buzz
summary: Ghent has medieval guild houses along canals, a moated castle and the Ghent Altarpiece, one of the world's great paintings. It's livelier and less crowded than Bruges, with a big student population, great bars and the Gentse Feesten festival in July.
seasonNote: Spring to early autumn is best. July brings the 10-day Gentse Feesten. December has a Christmas market.
arrival: Trains from Brussels take about 30 minutes, and from Bruges about 25.
gettingAround: Walk the centre; trams and bikes.
foodTip: Waterzooi stew, cuberdon sweets, fries and Belgian beer.

items.name: Gravensteen
items.summary: A moated 12th-century castle with a witty audio guide.

items.name: Ghent Altarpiece
items.summary: Van Eyck's 'Adoration of the Mystic Lamb', with a mixed-reality visitor centre.

items.name: Graslei and Korenlei
items.summary: Guild houses lining the canal, Ghent's postcard view.

items.name: Belfry
items.summary: A 91 m medieval belfry with a lift to the top.
items.tip: Go up for the three towers view.

items.name: Canal boat tour
items.summary: Boats through the medieval canals.

items.name: Patershol
items.summary: A maze of cobbled lanes full of restaurants.

items.name: Museum of Fine Arts
items.summary: Flemish masters from Bosch to Ensor, plus Van Eyck restoration work.

items.name: Waterzooi
items.summary: A creamy stew of chicken or fish with vegetables.

items.name: Cuberdons
items.summary: Cone-shaped raspberry sweets with a gooey centre.

items.name: Belgian beer bars
items.summary: Hundreds of beers in old bars like Dulle Griet.
items.tip: Order a Kwak in its special glass.
